items.title: Ruth Brown interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995
items.q: The interviewer mentions Miles Davis, but the interviewee (Ruth Brown) does not mention him or claim any personal interaction, only responding to the interviewer's statement about police harassment.

ctx.x: The funniest thing happened. Intuitiveness. When it’s about survival you think of something. I’ll never forget the band was playing and he leaned over the hood of the car and started playing on the hood of the car. And the police officers accepted that. He proved that he knew how to move his hands at least. And then last but not least, they looked at me and I would be standing there very arrogant in those days. I didn’t fear death, you understand? And they said, “And who are you?” And I was very vain and I said,…
You know there’s a classic case of the police harassing Miles Davis ‘cause he had his beautiful Ferrari, and he finally got this license plate that says “I own it.”

I own it, yes. Well those things occurred quite often. I had fire set to my car in Birmingham, you know. We’ve had occasions to be stopped and taken to what we call “night court” where the judge lived back in the woods somewhere, you didn’t go to the station you went to his house. And they tell you that you owed two hundred, three hundred dollars, and they wanted it right then and we had to pay it and all this, to move, you know. Those are some of the reasons that caused me to be a little vain and arrogant and…
